questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: Your attitude.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your overall driving behavior.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior during the road test.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side. It lets you watch passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help the driver see?

options.text: The danger zones near the front bumper.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones near the front bumper.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help you see the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides from the front to the service door.

questions.question: Why should you park at least 10 feet away from students when picking them up?

options.text: You can see their movements clearly.
It will be hard to get any closer.
Students need the exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Park with the front bumper at least 10 feet from students. This is safest because students must walk to the bus, and you can watch them the whole time.

questions.question: What does ABS allow a driver to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup and helps you stay in control when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Is backing a school bus recommended?

options.text: Yes, it is strongly encouraged.
No, it is strongly discouraged.
Only in the morning.

questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged. Only back up if there is no other safe option. Always follow proper safety steps if you must back up.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be positioned at the end of a basic vehicle controls skills test?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not doing so can result in failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should the driver do when approaching a school bus stop?

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: What should you do if stopped at a railroad crossing in a school bus?

options.text: Get ready to move as soon as the train passes.
Ignore the signs and signals.
Open the door to look and listen for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door to look and listen for trains.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on signals. Tell passengers to be quiet, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. Check both directions for trains before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What happens if your vehicle's ABS breaks?

options.text: You will have no brakes at all.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. If ABS breaks, your regular brakes will still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS.
Only have ABS if students under 10 years old will ride the bus.
May have ABS.

questions.explanation: Most school buses made after 1998 or 1999 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Many older buses have ABS too.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go back up after a train passes, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.explanation: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing and the gate does not go back up after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not try to drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: School bus doors should be closed while driving, except when:

options.text: Crossing railroad tracks.
You need to cool off the inside of the bus.
There is no vehicle next to the bus.

questions.explanation: School bus doors must stay closed anytime the bus is moving, except when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: Where should students stay during an emergency?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control if they stay on the bus rather than leave it. However, if staying on the bus puts students at risk, the driver should take them to a safe location.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides if you can proceed:

options.text: The driver.
A control device.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control device. The driver must decide when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Keep contact with the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.explanation: When exiting during a vehicle control test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must keep contact with the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, getting as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure they work properly and have grooved surfaces.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine to secure the bus when unloading students. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's seat. You must watch the students as they unload.

questions.question: Except for the straight line backing exercise, a driver may exit and check position up to:

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.explanation: You can exit to check your position during any test exercise. During straight line backing, you may look only once. During any other exercise, you may look twice.
